routeSelection.basis: The exact normalized target names English Language and Culture. Current official programme and adopted 2026–2027 EER confirm this specialization separately from American Studies. Retain the ordinary domestic pathway; do not substitute the conditional abroad/educational-minor replacement route. For the required 5-EC restricted choice, instantiate Adaptations: Page, Stage, Screen; for the 10-EC thesis choose English literature, the first listed thesis option. The 30-EC Arts-minor and 30-EC free-elective allocations remain genuine choice space, with their binding restrictions explicit. The restricted elective follows the first English-specialization-coded course in the adopted choice order (after the two American-Studies-coded entries); its selection does not depend on the UCR match.

core: Literary interpretation, genres, stylistics and creative expression
High and popular culture, historical society and English-speaking cultural worlds
questions: How cultural narratives represent identity, social relations and historical power

trace: directly teaches practical criticism, fiction, poetry, drama and narrative form, supplying the literary-analysis foundation
directly teaches argument, rhetorical theory and persuasive writing/speaking, contributing to the target communication strand without implying English-proficiency instruction

provides specific complementary modern historical study of industrialisation, sovereignty, war, welfare and decolonisation needed to interpret nineteenth-/twentieth-century cultural works; it is not British history alone

Directly develops close and comparative interpretation of world literary works from ancient epic to later fiction, including genre, narrative, colonial critique and modernist subjectivity. This supplies literary methods and cultural interpretation, not a dedicated British or American period survey.

Directly teaches linguistic stylistics across morphology, syntax, semantics, discourse, pragmatics and cognition, applying these frameworks in original textual analysis. This is substantive language analysis within the programme, but not a full structural, historical or English phonological sequence.
directly studies American gender histories through storybooks, interviews, queer cinema and cultural storytelling, contributing a defined cultural-history strand

Directly applies public-speaking, debate and storytelling pedagogy in community-engaged work with primary-school children, including iterative teaching design and reflection. This contributes rhetorical practice and an educational application; it does not provide secondary-school English teaching or a proficiency curriculum.

Provides a specific complementary comparative study of myth transmission, narrative patterns, focalization, gender and cross-cultural adaptation, situating the programme’s literary interpretation within wider narrative traditions.
directly develops film-form and representation analysis to study narratives as cultural production and responses to social change
provides specific complementary study of printed books and pre-digital media as material objects shaping the circulation of knowledge, communication and cultural memory
provides specific complementary theories of race, gender, class and institutions for analysing social relations represented in literature and media
directly studies memoir, autobiography, travel writing and cultural self-representation, including memory and identity in life narratives
directly examines American mainstream media and everyday life from television to TikTok, including storytelling, identity and whose accounts are heard

Directly studies Indigenous social and cultural histories, storytelling, colonial institutions, resistance and resurgence in North America through relational historical inquiry and arts-based collaboration. This contributes to critical study of English-speaking cultural worlds without relabelling Indigenous cultures as English culture.
directly analyses documentary histories, genres and the ethical representation of people, with an essay and short documentary production

Directly studies literary-to-film adaptation, narrative form, medium specificity and theory-led text/film research. This implements cross-media literary interpretation without claiming a fixed British set-text list.
directly studies race, systemic oppression and cultural representation in American history from the nineteenth century onward, including research-based podcast production
provides specific complementary analysis of imperial power and its historical rise/fall for studying English-speaking cultural worlds; it does not teach the historical spread of English itself
provides specific complementary theories of modernity, imperialism and colonial responses for interpreting cultural narratives and power, rather than generic social breadth
directly applies feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic approaches in a literary research project
directly studies and practices poetic form, voice, rhythm and performance through critical reading and creative projects

Provides a specific complementary contribution through historical research-question formulation, critical source inquiry and a substantial historical research paper, supporting the programme’s cultural-history investigations. The current course is Researching the “American Century”; no Walcheren expedition or particular British archive is claimed.

Makes a specific complementary contribution through philosophical theories of emotion, emotion and artistic expression, and close conceptual analysis, supporting interpretation of art and cultural responses. It is not a general philosophy-of-culture substitute.

alternatives.label: Literature, rhetoric & cultural history
alternatives.concept: Study literary form, linguistic stylistics, rhetoric and film alongside American cultural representation and source-based history. Social theory and the philosophy of emotion support focused analyses of identity, power and artistic response; a dedicated English-proficiency curriculum, structural and historical linguistics sequence, and the full British literary-period sequence remain gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: Six literature, four communication, five media and five history courses form the main curriculum; two sociology courses and Philosophy of Emotion supply specific complementary interpretation. The descriptive label fits this sustained literary/cultural response without promising the full English Studies discipline.
progression: All exact workbook terms and formal prerequisites pass. Literary introduction and stylistics precede advanced literary research; rhetoric precedes its practice module; film introduction precedes documentary and adaptation; introductory sociology precedes Modern Sociology; modern history precedes the source-based seminar. Level-three Philosophy of Emotion has no formal prerequisite and is placed in the final semester.

candidates.label: English structural, historical and global linguistics
Advanced English proficiency and language development
English in science, politics and business

selection.assessment: One coherent related-fields response materially addresses literary interpretation, linguistic stylistics, cultural production and representation, with 6 literature, 4 communication, 5 media and 5 history courses; it is not merely general humanities breadth. Literature/culture is already substantively covered and gives no second distinct concept. The first additional structural/historical/global English-linguistics direction was tested against Style & Meaning (actual syntax, semantics, discourse, pragmatics and cognition) and Psycholinguistics (acquisition, bilingualism, speech processing and hands-on experiments), brain/behaviour foundations and research methods. These are positive contributions, but cannot supply a coherent 24-course response to English structure, variation, phonology and historical development; generic psychology or computing substitutions would change its defining subject. Advanced proficiency lacks a dedicated development sequence despite genuine rhetorical, academic and creative writing. Science/politics/business describes English-language use, not three curricular specializations. Teaching was tested through primary-school rhetorical teaching, Psycholinguistics, brain/behaviour and Lifespan Developmental Psychology; these do not establish an English-learning/secondary pedagogy programme. Rejection is substantive, not the lack of a teaching licence. Stop after the first failed additional concept; subsequent retained tests document coverage, not a third alternative.

blocks: Both directly teach literary interpretation and critical reading; the UCR introduction covers more than English literature.
Both study adaptation of literary texts across media. UCR concentrates on text-to-film analysis and adaptation theory; the selected external elective also includes stage adaptation.

Both support research in literary studies. UCR applies critical perspectives in a textual research project; it does not cover the seminar’s full English-language-and-culture scope or replace the bachelor’s thesis.

Both address linguistic description and analysis. UCR applies grammar, semantics, discourse and cognition to textual interpretation; this is a substantive part of introductory language analysis, not a complete general linguistics curriculum.
Both develop oral communication; UCR focuses on rhetorical argument rather than English-language proficiency.
The UCR course directly studies American popular-media narratives and social life, one important part of the British/American component; it does not supply British popular-culture coverage.
External English specialization, choices & independent research

Both develop academic writing and presentation. UCR teaches scholarly-source evaluation, literature synthesis and research introductions alongside reflective and civic work; it does not reproduce English-specific proficiency assessment.

The selected programme develops scholarly and creative writing, but no course provides the dedicated English-language development of Writing English. PPD is placed with Academic Communication Skills, its stronger specific educational function.

Modern History and History of Empires provide comparative historical interpretation, not the sustained British-history subject of this component; the current history research seminar supplies no verified British case.
No selected course teaches the English speech-sound/pronunciation training that defines this component.
Philosophy of Emotion contributes focused emotion and art theory; that narrower topic does not establish the primary philosophy-of-culture content of this component.
World literary comparison, life narratives and American media history contribute related methods and cultural subjects, but none establishes a sustained survey of American literature.

Style & Meaning substantively applies syntax within wider stylistic analysis and is placed with Introduction to Linguistics. No other selected course independently supplies this English syntax component; it is not duplicated across rows.
No selected course provides the historical development of English; comparative imperial history is not historical linguistics.
Great Literary Works offers world-literary comparison and modernist interpretation rather than a sustained nineteenth-/twentieth-century British literary-period survey.
The selected literary courses teach genre, interpretation and critical approaches, not a sustained seventeenth-/eighteenth-century British literary survey.
History of Empires supplies historical context, but no selected course directly studies the global linguistic spread and varieties of English.
No selected course supplies the systematic phonological study of English; poetic sound and rhetorical delivery do not establish that linguistic content.
No selected course provides Middle English literature in its historical-language and literary setting; comparative myth is not a substitute.

No selected course supplies second-language-acquisition research. Psycholinguistics has genuine acquisition content but belongs to the separately assessed, rejected additional concept and is not scheduled here.

The literary curriculum includes drama and adaptation, but no selected course establishes sustained early-modern stage study; ancient tragedy and general film adaptation are different primary subjects.
PPD supports academic and personal development, but is already placed with academic communication. No selected course independently supplies English/American Studies-specific career orientation.
The required 10-EC English-literature thesis remains distinct from course research projects. UCR optional independent research is displayed separately in this row, outside the scheduled180EC.

notes.text: Radboud combines advanced English proficiency, linguistics and sustained British and other Anglophone literary study with independent research. This UCR programme offers substantial literary, stylistic and cultural analysis through literature, rhetoric, media and history. Its grammar, discourse analysis and academic writing are meaningful contributions, while dedicated English-proficiency development, phonetics, phonology, historical-English study and the full British literary-period sequence remain gaps.

audience.programmeDescription: Explore English language, literature and culture through language development, linguistics, British and other English-speaking literary traditions, and independent research. The English Language and Culture track is distinct from American Studies.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This UCR programme offers sustained literary interpretation, linguistic stylistics, creative expression, film and cultural history. These subjects respond to important parts of English Studies. Its language analysis and academic writing provide partial correspondences; it does not reproduce the dedicated English-proficiency, structural and historical linguistics curriculum or the full British literary-period sequence.
